recipes.name: Tasty Lentil Tacos
ingredients_raw: 1 tablespoon taco seasoning, or to taste

steps.text: Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add onion and garlic; cook and stir until tender, about 5 minutes. Add lentils and taco seasoning; cook and stir 1 minute.
Add chicken broth; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer until lentils are tender, 25 to 30 minutes.
Uncover the skillet; cook until mixture is slightly thickened, 6 to 8 minutes. Mash lentils slightly; stir in salsa.
Serve about 1/4 cup lentil mixture in each taco shell.

raw_recipe.headline: Tasty Lentil Tacos
raw_recipe.description: This tasty lentil taco recipe is healthy, too. It combines onion, garlic, taco seasoning, lentils, broth, and salsa. Serve with your favorite toppings.

review.reviewBody: This is so much better than it has any right to be, and has quickly become one of my favorite recipes! It's very friendly to dietary restrictions and easily becomes vegan. Be sure to stir in the salsa with the lentils at the end... it has a significant impact on the overall flavor and texture.

I made this recipe as is and had a couple issues, the lentils were no way tender enough after cooking and the flavor was slightly bland.....I used a full bag of lentils and it made a good amount so I took the leftovers, put them in my slow cooker, added a can of corn and a can of black beans (both cans 12.5 oz and completely drained) then I added more chicken broth, added water and added more taco seasoning. I set it to low and left it over night. In the morning I tasted it, added some more water (being careful to only add what I thought would cook off) added more seasoning and let it cook on low until lunch and tried again. I felt it was a million times better, the beans were very tender and it was hard to believe there was no meat in the mixture.

This is a great recipe! Finally a healthy meal everyone in my family will eat! And when i say everyone I mean my picky 6yo. I made this in the instant pot and it was so fast and easy. I used the saute function for the steps up to adding the chicken stock, then I switched to pressure cook for 12 minutes with a 10 minute natural release. We live at altitude and increase all cooking times by 30%, so decrease time if you're closer to sea level. It had a little too much liquid with this method, but it was nothing a little cornstarch couldn't fix.

This was VERY good. My husband was really leery of this one, but he ate it anyway. After the first bite, I got a thumbs up. I used beef bouillon only because I was out of chicken stock. I threw in a jalapeño cuz it was going south in the refrigerator and I used the taco seasoning mix recipe on AR because I don't like all the additives and preservatives of store-bought. I cooked the lentil mixture in my Insta Pot for 23 minutes on Manuel. At the last, I added the salsa which was my own home made habanero salsa. Can you tell I like it spicy? It was very good. It will be my go to taco recipe from now on. Thanks!

I just tried this for the first time, my 12 year old wants to experiment with vegetarian meals. First off, a disclaimer, I used an Instant Pot pressure cooker rather than stovetop so modified the cook time, liquid, and also used about 25% pot barley, the rest was green lentils. Also used homemade taco seasoning. 

After reading in reviews it was 'soupy' I tried 25 minutes with equal amounts of water to lentil/barley (broth would have been tastier, that's what i normally use for beans but kid wants vegetarian). Not enough liquid, and lentils were hard. Added another cup of water, cooked another 10 minutes. Much better! I also added some seasoned/cooked black beans after cooking, mashed it up a bit. My son had a hard time believing there was no meat. This will be a staple even if we're not eating vegetarian!

I made this in the Instant Pot! I sautéed the onions and garlic using the sauté function, then added the lentils, broth and salsa and pressure cooked for thirty minutes. Once it was done it was a little liquidy so I put it back on sauté and cooked off some of the liquid.

These are awesome! I made the recipe with the change of sauteing the onion/garlic in extra virgin coconut oil, as I never use canola. Also just used a whole onion instead of measuring out 1 cup. The lentils took 40 min before they were tender, and I didn't mash them at all. Love this recipe, and it will become a regular!
Update-since I can be lazy cook I now just use canned lentils that I rinse and drain making for a super quick meal!

Delicious, cheap & healthy! I like spicy food so I added a dash of cayenne pepper and a few splashes of hot sauce and it's awesome. As some others said, it took longer to cook and required more liquid than this recipe calls for - took about 45 min total and a lot more water. 

Edit: Maybe those lentils were old or a different brand. My new bag takes closer to the recommended cooking time, maybe just a few minutes over. My husband LOVES this recipe! I've started making a double batch on the weekend to eat during the week since it reheats so well. I also froze some once, texture wasn't perfect after but flavor was still great.

This was phenomenal! It was my first time making lentils and now I don't know if I can eat tacos any other way! I used unsalted chicken broth and low sodium taco mix to cut down on the sodium, and this recipe was still spectacularly flavorful. This has definitely been added to my list of staple meals. I did end up cooking my lentils for about 45 minutes though as at 30 minutes they were not yet tender and still had lots of liquid around them.

I agree with other cooks on here, the cooking time was too short for the lentils, it took about 45 mins for them to soften up. I used vegetable broth and drained the lentils after cooking. I then added a seasoning packet of Taco bell seasoning mix to them. This is a great recipe when you feel like eating crispy tacos but no longer want to eat meat, I will be making this again

We used 6 inch flour tortillas (warmed at 350 for 10 minutes), and topped the lentil mix with shredded cheese, sour cream, and chopped cilantro. Excellent and filling at 3 tacos each, and the size we made them, it was enough for 9 tacos. Very affordable, too: my cost was maybe $5 for the entire dish. I will definitely be making this again and again!

Lentils took a very long time and extra liquid to soften. About 1-1/2 hours simmering and stirring, added an extra cup of broth over that time. Tasting as they cooked, they were pretty bland. Ended up using a whole envelope of taco seasoning, plus some additional garlic powder, cumin and salt. I did follow the recipe exactly until taste tests revealed it was much too bland. Don’t skip the salsa. It’s necessary! With those minor tweaks, this is absolutely delicious, budget friendly, kids loved it. Will definitely make again.

Just made this recipe for meal prep! I agree with the comments that say to cook the lentils longer and with more water, I ended up beefing it up by adding a can of black beans, green chiles, some tomato paste (I had very little salsa available), some lime juice, extra tavo seasoning, and some hot sauce of choice. It was great 👍
I have never cooked lentils! Wow, this was so good and easy!
Really good. Definitely a recipe I'll do again!

The end result is delicious, however, like some other users noted the lentils took much longer to cook. Additionally I had to use much more liquid to achieve softened lentils without scorching them. I wish I measured but I just kept adding some liquid every 10 minutes or so until softened.

Myb this is a US thing just like you guys call melted cheese “queso” which just means “cheese”. But what do you mean by salsa? (Tht just means sauce) a what salsa? Tomato based? Bell Pepper based? White sauce?
Delish! My hubby loved it too and we will definitely make these again.
Love these tacos, I omitted the corn, but love them, very filling
This is a staple in my vegetarian household. We use vegetable broth. So good. And so easy on a weeknight. Thank you.
